clusters.name: Your grandfather Walter's move to Sorrel Valley, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around the time your grandfather moved the family across the country and bought the orchard in March 1952, within the next year: your grandmother June grew homesick and wrote to her sister every day, your grandfather stayed out in the trees and kept his distance from June, your father got into fights at school and was sent home twice, your grandfather stopped writing to his brother after a quarrel over their father's land money, your grandmother kept to her bed for weeks that winter, your grandfather and grandmother rowed over money for new trees, and by September your grandmother joined the church choir and her letters thinned out. The shifts show a family in difficulty with the move and its aftermath, settling as your grandmother found her footing in the new place.

clusters.name: Your grandfather Walter's orchard failing, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the time the orchard failed and the bank called in the loan in May 1968, within the next year: your grandfather drank heavily most nights, your grandfather and father blamed each other for the loan, your father took over the family's money and talks with the bank, your brother Carl's asthma attacks grew worse that winter, you began wetting the bed again in April 1969, your grandmother Ida was found to have heart trouble and told to stop working at the bakery, and by October your grandfather stopped drinking and took work pruning other men's trees. The orchard's loss and the family's move to Ridgeport brought shifts across the household as your father stepped in and your grandfather struggled.

clusters.name: Your father Glen's job loss at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around the time your father lost his job when the Ridgeport cannery closed in February 1975, within the next year: your father sat out in the truck in the yard for hours most of that year, your parents fought loud fights over money at night, your mother took a second job cleaning offices at night, you stopped eating properly and lost weight that summer, you kept to your room and said little to your mother, your grandfather Walter drank again after six years off it, and by June 1976 you were eating again and made the track team. Your father's loss brought shifts through the household that settled once he found work driving the delivery truck.

clusters.name: Your partner's mother Wilma moving in, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around the time Wilma sold her farm and moved into your house in January 1990, within the next year and a half: you clashed with her over the children's bedtimes and meals, Hollis worked late and kept out of the kitchen rows, Hollis took his mother's side, your son Owen had tantrums at preschool and was sent home twice, Wilma took over Lily's care, you developed eczema on both hands, you and Hollis rowed most nights, and Wilma took a flat in town in June 1991; by August your eczema cleared. The months of conflict and distance in the household settled once Wilma moved out.

clusters.name: Your sister Tess's drinking, 1996–1997
clusters.reason: Around the time your sister Tess began drinking most nights in October 1996, within the next few months: you phoned her every night and worried for her, you and your mother paid her rent and kept your nephew Jesse most weekends, and Tess and her husband Rick had shouting matches with Rick sleeping at his brother's for a month; by June 1997 Tess stopped drinking and went to meetings twice a week. Your worry for your sister and your mother's help brought shifts in the family that eased once Tess steadied.
